claim_text: Across five LLM tutor families (Claude, Llama, Gemini, Qwen, GPT) tested against simulated gaming/wheel-spinning/off-task learner states, relative tutor rankings held stable but absolute support quality varied by state, and automated tutor scoring did not fully match human judgment.
quote_location: Abstract: 'relative rankings remained stable across learner states and interaction lengths, while absolute performance varied...Human validation further showed that automated tutor evaluation does not fully align with human judgment.'

claim_text: An LLM-driven spaced-repetition scheduler, evaluated only against 100 simulated learners over 100 simulated days (not real humans), scored a 90.2% vs. 88.4% simulated success-rate edge over the best non-LLM baseline (SSP-MMC).
quote_location: Abstract: 'LECTOR achieves a 90.2% success rate compared to 88.4% for the best baseline (SSP-MMC)'

claim_text: Problem-based/project-style practice outperformed conventional instruction on long-term retention and on measures of skill development, across the meta-analyses this synthesis compared.
quote_location: abstract (Semantic Scholar API): 'PBL was superior when it comes to long-term retention, skill development and satisfaction of students and teachers'

claim_text: Conventional/drill-style instruction beat problem-based practice on short-term retention measured by standardized exams -- the reverse ranking from the long-term outcome.
quote_location: abstract (Semantic Scholar API): 'traditional approaches were more effective for short-term retention as measured by standardized board exams'

claim_text: Pooling 46 effect sizes / 30 studies (12,585 students, 189 schools, 9 countries), project-based learning produced a medium-to-large achievement gain over traditional instruction, d+=0.71.
quote_location: abstract (Semantic Scholar API): 'the overall mean weighted effect size (d+) was 0.71...medium to large positive effect'

claim_text: The same meta-analysis found the project-based-learning advantage moderated by subject area, school location, instructional hours and IT support, but not by educational stage or small-group size -- one unit design, similar effect across grade levels in this pooled sample.
quote_location: abstract (Semantic Scholar API): 'the mean effect size was affected by subject area, school location, hours of instruction, and information technology support, but not by educational stage and small group size'

claim_text: Across 108 controlled evaluations, mastery-learning programs (practice segmented into units gated by a proficiency criterion before advancing, rather than fixed time) raised exam performance for college, high-school and upper-elementary students.
quote_location: ERIC EJ415887 abstract: 'meta-analysis of findings from 108 controlled evaluations showed that mastery learning programs have positive effects on the examination performance of students'

claim_text: Simulation-based mastery learning -- practicing a clinical skill in discrete units until a fixed proficiency threshold, not for fixed time -- produced measured downstream transfer across 23 medical-education studies: improved patient-care practices, patient outcomes, and collateral effects beyond the training lab.
quote_location: PubMed abstract, PMID 24606621: 'Measured outcomes have been achieved in educational laboratories (T1), and as improved patient care practices (T2), patient outcomes (T3) and collateral effects (T4)'

claim_text: In a 2x2 RCT (93 students) that experimentally induced novice vs. 'expert' status before instruction, adding instructional explanations to a practice unit reversed benefit by expertise on a transfer test, but the same reversal did not hold on a retention test of the same material.
quote_location: ERIC EJ999802 abstract: 'The expertise reversal effect was replicated for the dependent measure transfer, but not for retention'

claim_text: In an RCT (104 college accounting students), pre-decomposing a complex problem into isolated sub-parts helped novices and hurt more knowledgeable learners, and only for high-complexity material -- the right grain size of a practice unit depends jointly on the learner's prior knowledge and the material's complexity.
quote_location: ERIC EJ1119955 abstract: 'isolated elements beneficial for novices, while interacting elements were appropriate for more knowledgeable learners...only for high rather than low element interactivity materials'

claim_text: Applied to 351 introductory-Java students' actual code submissions, naive methods for automatically discovering a programming problem's underlying knowledge components (the practice-unit boundaries) performed poorly; a purpose-built model produced components whose learning curves fit the expected power-law-of-practice shape better and better predicted submission correctness than four baselines.
quote_location: ERIC ED630850 abstract: 'identifying KCs with naive methods is a difficult task...our learning curves exhibit a substantially better curve fit'

claim_text: The same meta-synthesis found project-based/problem-based practice produced higher satisfaction among both students and teachers than conventional instruction, across the meta-analyses it compared.
quote_location: abstract (Semantic Scholar API): 'PBL was superior when it comes to...satisfaction of students and teachers'

claim_text: In a school-based CPR retention meta-analysis, continuous compression-metric changes were statistically non-significant at 2-8 months while pass/fail correct-technique success rates swung from 86.9% to 12.81%, showing instrument choice (continuous vs threshold) changes the apparent retention curve.
quote_location: Results, "Mean chest compression depth" section: "a large change in success rates was observed in long-term follow-ups, from 86.9% to 12.81% after 6-8 months"

claim_text: Across the same meta-analysis's included studies, immediate post-training correct-CPR-performance rates ranged 74-90%, the baseline any later decay must be read against -- a single training session already yields majority-correct performance before any retention interval elapses.
quote_location: Abstract: "rates of correct CPR performance ranging from 74% to 90% across various components"

claim_text: The same review found performance and detection bias -- not selection bias -- as the dominant quality problem across studies measuring long-term CPR retention: the instruments/observers assessing decayed skill were the weakest methodological link, not randomization.
quote_location: "Overall quality of data": "risk of performance and detection biases was detected in most of the included studies"

claim_text: A quasi-experimental single-group study of 37 final-year medical students found significant decay in a written knowledge test from immediate to 6-month posttest despite training, but never assessed hands-on resuscitation performance -- knowledge retention stood in for skill retention.
quote_location: Abstract: "there was improved knowledge even after 6 months...there was decay in knowledge"

claim_text: A 1,344-effect-size meta-regression estimates half of initial skill-acquisition gains are lost after ~6.5 months (accuracy-based) versus ~13 months (speed-based) of nonuse, treating retention interval as continuous rather than the field's earlier categorical short/long split.
quote_location: Abstract: "half of initial skill acquisition performance gains were lost after approximately 6.5 months for accuracy, 13 months for speed"

claim_text: The same meta-analysis flags a design confound specific to retention instruments: a delayed test itself lets learners relearn during the probe, so raw pre/post differences conflate true retention with in-test relearning unless a design isolates the two.
quote_location: Abstract: "the need to isolate retention performance from relearning effects...when interpreting changes in performance over time"

claim_text: In a 1,713-student measurement-invariance study, self-reported learning gains associated most strongly with perceived institutional/pedagogical conditions and only secondarily with cognitive-engagement indicators -- self-report of gains tracks environment more than the cognition it claims to measure.
quote_location: Abstract: "Supportive Environment and Effective Teaching Practices were most strongly associated with self-reported learning gains, whereas cognitive indicators played a secondary role"

claim_text: A 2026 preprint proposes replacing the single collapsed 'prompting score' for AI-assisted work with three separately assessable competencies (Framing, Judging, Steering), arguing unaided-performance tests still dominate schools while the actually-needed skill goes unmeasured in its own right.
quote_location: Abstract: "Schools still measure unaided performance, yet the real task is to produce good work with AI...rarely assessed in its own right"

claim_text: A construct-validity argument holds that as real-world English-use domains increasingly involve generative AI, the extrapolation from a standardized unaided-performance test score to 'communicative readiness' becomes progressively less defensible -- a transfer-validity problem, not a scoring or security problem.
quote_location: Abstract: "the extrapolation from unaided test performance to academic communicative readiness becomes less self-evident"

claim_text: A 1993 assessment-cost proposal argues matrix sampling -- testing only a low proportion of both students and tasks per administration -- can make constructed-response/performance assessment affordable at scale, trading individual-level precision for population-level measurement at a fraction of per-task cost.
quote_location: ERIC abstract: "Matrix sampling, featuring low-proportion sampling of both students and assessment tasks, may offer a cost-effective solution"

claim_text: Two experiments (N=610, N=871) found a scalable, facilitator-free calibration-feedback training method (the Practical scoring rule) produced no improvement in confidence calibration over control or plain outcome-feedback, despite being designed for domain-general, low-cost deployment.
quote_location: Abstract: "We found no improvement in calibration due to either training regime"

claim_text: A confirmatory-factor-analysis validation (n=1,960 adult distance learners) produced a psychometrically sound self-directed-learning diagnostic instrument, but validity here means internal factor fit, not any demonstrated link to actually-sustained independent study behavior.
quote_location: Crossref abstract: "confirmatory factor analysis showed that the final model...has a good fit on the data, thus affirming the strong validity and reliability of the tool"

claim_text: Two major deployed intelligent tutoring systems operationalize 'unproductive struggle' (wheel-spinning) with a fixed mastery-and-timeliness threshold: a student must answer correctly on three consecutive opportunities to demonstrate mastery, and must do so within a bounded number of opportunities (10 in ASSISTments, 15 in Cognitive Tutor/MATHia) or is classified as wheel-spinning on that skill.
quote_location: PMC full text, 'Wheel Spinning and Unproductive Persistence' section; 'a student must respond correctly to three consecutive opportunities to demonstrate mastery... timeliness corresponds to a student reaching mastery within ten opportunities... (10 in ASSISTments; 15 in Cognitive Tutor)'

claim_text: In a university ITS lab course, making hints available at no scoring penalty versus penalizing hint use produced statistically significant differences in how often students requested hints, but only for exercises where baseline hint-request rates were neither very high nor very low; the effect was moderated by problem type and difficulty, not uniform across all exercises.
quote_location: pdf p.2-3, Tables 1-2 and Conclusions; 'There were several statistically significant differences in the number of hint requests between the hinting technique of having penalties for selecting hints or not... depending on the type and difficulty of the problem.'

claim_text: In log data from a middle-school ITS, students' negative affect (boredom, frustration) predicted more hint-seeking in the following unit, and whether hint use helped or hurt subsequent performance flipped sign depending on the co-occurring affect state rather than being uniformly beneficial or harmful.
quote_location: pdf p.6-7 Results; 'every unit increase in Frustration led to a slight effect where Hints per Step predicted an increase of .039 on subsequent performance' vs. 'Frustration predicted an even poorer subsequent performance in unit 5 than Hint use alone.'

claim_text: In a randomized online experiment, both human-tutor-authored and ChatGPT-generated algebra hints produced positive pre-to-post learning gains, but only the human-authored hints' gain was statistically significant; ChatGPT-hint learning gains were substantially and significantly lower than human-hint gains in both algebra topic areas tested.
quote_location: arXiv abstract/results, fetched directly; '70% of hints produced by ChatGPT passed our manual quality checks and that both human and ChatGPT conditions produced positive learning gains. However, gains were only statistically significant for human tutor created hints.'

claim_text: Across a multi-semester analysis of 999 K-12 math students using an ITS, two simple behavioral indicators of unproductive hint use -- requesting a hint too soon after starting a problem, and reading a hint superficially -- were consistently associated with reduced learning gains across cohorts, holding after controlling for prior knowledge and strongest for lower-prior-knowledge learners.
quote_location: Semantic Scholar abstract (primary ACM text paywalled, not read this round); 'simple, interpretable indicators of unproductive hint use—premature hint requests and superficial hint reading—are consistently associated with reduced learning gains across cohorts... particularly pronounced among learners with lower prior knowledge.'

claim_text: A systematic review of 19 purposively designed studies (8 RCTs, 5 quasi-experiments, 6 observational evaluations) on the Hawthorne effect found most studies reported some evidence that being observed/studied changes behavior, but the studies were so heterogeneous that the conditions under which the effect operates, its mechanisms, and its magnitude remain largely unknown after 60 years of the construct's use.
quote_location: PMC3969247 full text, Abstract/'What is new'; 'Most of the 19 purposively designed evaluation studies... provide some evidence of research participation effects. The heterogeneity of these studies means that little can be confidently inferred about the size of these effects, the conditions under which they operate, or their mechanisms.'

claim_text: In a multiple-baseline study alternating observer-present and observer-absent conditions while teachers received performance feedback on implementing a classwide behavior plan, no difference in treatment integrity was found between observed and unobserved conditions -- improvement was attributable to the performance feedback itself, not to being watched.
quote_location: PMC2521856 full text, Abstract; 'examining reactivity using a multiple baseline design with alternating treatments for observer-present and observer-absent conditions... No differences were found between conditions, and treatment integrity improved across all teachers, suggesting that performance feedback, rather than observer reactivity, was responsible for reported behavior changes.'

claim_text: Across three lab experiments on a copying task, deliberately increasing the effort/cost of re-accessing needed information (rather than leaving it always visible) improved participants' ability to resume the task correctly after an interruption, at the cost of slower task completion -- supporting higher, not lower, information-access cost as a design lever against interruption-caused forgetting.
quote_location: Semantic Scholar abstract (secondary; primary PDF host unreachable this round); 'increasing information access cost... encourages a more memory-intensive strategy... High IAC facilitated resumption after interruption... The main disadvantage of a high access cost was a reduction in speed of task completion.'

claim_text: Across three experiments, practicing an interruption-and-resumption sequence sped up subsequent resumption only when the same specific primary-task/interruption-task pairing was practiced again; practice on the primary task alone, or on a different interruption pairing, did not transfer -- interruption-recovery training is task-pair-specific, not a general skill.
quote_location: ERIC abstract (public-domain metadata; primary APA PDF paywalled, not read this round); 'people were able to resume a primary task faster only when they had previous practice with that specific primary and interruption task-pair. Experience with other primary and interruption task-pairs, or practice on the primary task alone, did not facilitate resumption.'

claim_text: In a study of 229 students given a procedural task interrupted for three different durations, higher working-memory capacity sharply reduced the time cost of resuming after longer interruptions, while lower-WMC individuals suffered substantially larger resumption delays as interruption length grew.
quote_location: ERIC abstract (public-domain metadata; primary APA PDF paywalled, not read this round); 'individuals with high WMC experienced small increases in resumption lag as interruption duration increased, whereas individuals with low WMC experienced substantial increases in resumption lag as interruption duration increased.'

claim_text: CoMeT (support that rises on learner failure and fades on take-up, holding metacognitive demand constant) delivered a completed artifact twice as often as an unrestricted AI assistant while matching a question-only tutor's metacognitive demand and frustrating learners less, across three within-subject Python tasks (n=131 adults); the design explicitly could not test whether this affects retention.
quote_location: Abstract: 'CoMeT matched the question-only tutor's demand, delivered artifacts twice as often as the assistant, and frustrated learners less than the question-only tutor'; Section 9 (Scope and Further Work): 'whether contingent support affects retention is the question this design is least able to answer'

claim_text: Metacognitive feedback that makes the cost of offloading to an LLM explicit reduced answer-offloading during assisted practice (OR=0.47) and improved a subsequent unaided test (OR=1.51, 95% CI [0.98,2.33]); an effort-based reward manipulation had no detectable effect on either outcome. Both outcomes were measured immediately, not after a delay.
quote_location: Abstract: 'Metacognitive feedback reduced answer offloading (OR = 0.47) and improved test performance (OR = 1.51)'; Discussion (p.19): 'Our study assessed unaided performance immediately after a brief practice session... it remains unclear whether these effects translate into durable skill acquisition'

claim_text: Across three randomized controlled trials (N=1,222) on math and reading-comprehension tasks, brief (~10-minute) AI assistance caused participants to perform worse and skip more problems on a subsequent unassisted set than controls, even though the AI improved performance while available; the authors explicitly state they cannot speak to the durability of the effect because testing was immediate.
quote_location: Abstract: 'although AI assistance improves performance in the short-term, people perform significantly worse without AI and are more likely to give up... these effects emerge after only brief interactions with AI (approximately 10 minutes)'; Limitations (~p.12): 'we cannot speak to the durability of these effects: participants were tested immediately'

claim_text: Students randomized to a Socratic-Guidance (SG) LLM tutor versus a Prompt-Refinement (PR) tutor across a 6-week graduate robotics course showed greater within-session learning gains by the final guided session (interaction effect beta=0.72, p=.01), and weeks later, during an unconstrained-LLM course project, were more likely to adopt 'understanding-driven' prompting patterns (13/32 SG vs 4/25 PR, chi-sq=8.14, p=.017); groups with more understanding-driven prompters scored higher on project understanding (beta=1.30, p=.025).
quote_location: Section 4.2 (p.9): 'showed significantly greater gains from pre- to post-test than students in the PR condition (interaction effect: beta = 0.72, p = 0.01)'; Section 4.4 (p.11): 'students from the SG condition were more likely to enact Understanding-driven prompting patterns (nSG = 13, nPR = 4)... chi2 = 8.14, p = 0.017'

claim_text: Pooled AI tutoring (13 different AI tutors) produced learning gains on unaided GRE questions, after one hour of tutoring, statistically equivalent to expert human tutoring (p=.015), with the best-performing AI tutor beating the human tutor in 5 of 7 GRE domains; in a second comparison, one AI tutor's generated lesson plans and practice problems were rated by expert human tutors as producing equivalent learning gains (p=.044) at roughly 918x lower cost.
quote_location: Introduction (p.2): 'we show that pooled AI tutoring and human tutoring produced statistically equivalent learning gains (p=.015)'; Abstract: 'one AI tutor achieved learning gains equivalent to human tutoring... at approximately 918x lower cost'

claim_text: In a randomized field experiment in a graduate finance course, a pedagogically structured AI tutor produced larger gains than unrestricted consumer-AI access on the instructor's own course-final exam (all 86 randomized students, +2.6 of 100 points, same direction as the primary written-reasoning measure, where relational-quality answers rose from 8% to 49% in the tutored arm vs 8% to 27% in the holdout); voice interaction nearly doubled engagement and cost 2.8x more than text but produced learning statistically equivalent to text.
quote_location: Abstract (p.1): 'the instructor's own final, on file for all 86 randomized students, shows the same direction (2.6 points of 100...)'; 'the share of answers reaching relational quality rose from 8% to 49% in the tutored arm against 8% to 27% in the holdout'

claim_text: In a 4-week multisite RCT of an AI tutoring platform against business-as-usual self-directed revision, students allocated to the platform scored higher on curriculum-aligned post-tests (Hedges' g=0.33, 95% CI 0.18-0.48), with positive effects across all three science subjects tested and no differential impact by disadvantage status; attrition was substantial (30.7%) and the authors call the findings preliminary.
quote_location: Abstract: 'students allocated to Medly achieved higher post-test attainment than students undertaking business-as-usual self-directed revision (Hedges' g = 0.33, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.48)'

claim_text: Algorithmically-timed push notifications produced higher daily practice-adherence during a 9-week language-learning program (82% compliance) than self-scheduled reminders (67%) or no notifications (49%), but adherence in the notification group fell sharply once notifications stopped, consistent with an extrinsic rather than intrinsic habit.
quote_location: Abstract (Crossref record): 'the push notification group demonstrated significantly higher daily practice adherence (82% compliance) compared to the self-scheduled (67%) and control groups (49%)... a sharp decline in consistency for the notification group once reminders ceased, suggesting extrinsic dependency'

claim_text: In an observational study of a deployed intelligent tutor voluntarily used by adult learners at a technical college, tutor usage was associated with within-tutor skill improvement on knowledge components and with higher scores on separate course assessments taken after tutor use, suggesting transfer beyond the tutor itself.
quote_location: Abstract: 'we found evidence that this learning transferred outside the tutor, as observed through higher course assessment scores following tutor usage'

claim_text: No study has yet measured what happens to a skill after AI assistance is withdrawn: whether an AI-induced performance deficit washes out, plateaus, or reverses within days-to-weeks post-withdrawal is, as of this paper, an open empirical question; the paper proposes but has not executed a 3-arm, 3-domain, 22-week longitudinal protocol to answer it.
quote_location: Abstract (p.1): 'When the assistant is withdrawn for days or weeks, does the deficit wash out on its own, plateau at a permanently lower level, hide until a stress test exposes it, or reverse into gains... We call this unmeasured post-withdrawal phase cognitive washout'

claim_text: A randomized controlled trial of GPT-4-powered virtual tutoring (Microsoft Copilot) for English-language learning in Nigerian secondary schools found a 0.31 SD gain on a combined assessment (0.23 SD on English specifically) after six weeks, an effect the authors equate to roughly 1.5-2 years of business-as-usual schooling gains, with larger effects for female students and higher-baseline-ability students.
quote_location: ERIC description: 'The intervention demonstrated a significant improvement of 0.31 standard deviation on an assessment... The effect on English, the main outcome of interest, was of 0.23 standard deviations... equating to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling'

claim_text: A cross-sectional survey of 143 knowledge workers across five countries found that individual entrepreneurial orientation predicted deeper GenAI collaboration, which predicted GenAI dependence, which was associated with perceived erosion of professional skills; all measures are self-report, not tested performance.
quote_location: Abstract: 'Survey data from 143 knowledge workers across five countries are broadly consistent with this account'; 'dependence in turn is associated with perceived erosion of professional skills'

claim_text: A recurrent-neural-network diagnostic model (Deep Knowledge Tracing) predicted held-out student-response correctness far more accurately than the standard Bayesian Knowledge Tracing model used to diagnose learner mastery: AUC 0.85 vs 0.68 on Khan Academy data and 0.86 vs 0.69 on the Assistments dataset.
quote_location: "an LSTM neural network model led to an AUC of 0.85 which was a notable improvement over the performance of a standard BKT (AUC = 0.68)" (Results, p.6)

claim_text: Standard Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, the dominant diagnosis model this literature builds on, structurally assumes a skill once learned is never forgotten -- a limitation the newer neural diagnosis model does not remove but the paper flags explicitly.
quote_location: "The formulation of the original model assumed that once a skill is learned it is never forgotten." (Sec. 2.1, p.2)

claim_text: Diagnosing whether a student's answer is merely correct is much easier for current models than diagnosing which specific concept the student is missing: LLMs and knowledge-tracing baselines reach 63-70% accuracy on correctness prediction but only 2-17% Macro-F1 on concept-level deficiency prediction over the same data.
quote_location: "Llama-4 and o3-mini achieve Macro-F1 scores of only 5.43% and 2.16%, respectively" against correctness accuracies of 68.81% and 70.35% (Table 5 / Sec. 5.2)

claim_text: A zero-shot LLM asked to directly classify a student's misconception from dialogue, over a realistic label space (546 distinct misconceptions), performed worse than simple keyword matching -- naive LLM misconception diagnosis has a sharp accuracy limit at this label-space scale.
quote_location: "the zero-shot LLM classification baseline scores poorly, likely due to struggling to handle the large context with 546 unique misconceptions" (Sec. 5.1)

claim_text: Adding a generate-then-rerank pipeline (fine-tuned LLM proposes candidate misconceptions, a second fine-tuned LLM reranks them) improved misconception-diagnosis accuracy over direct classification or embedding-only baselines across most base models tested.
quote_location: "reranking improves the final predicted misconceptions ... for Claude Sonnet 4.5 including the reranking stage improves all metrics" (Sec. 5.3)

claim_text: A simple prompting framework that grounds an LLM programming tutor's feedback in a catalog of common student misconceptions (rather than generic feedback) was, in a real classroom deployment, more pedagogically oriented and more satisfying to students than ungrounded feedback.
quote_location: "even simple prompting frameworks can meaningfully steer tutor behavior to be more pedagogically oriented and noticeably more satisfying to students" (abstract, Semantic Scholar record; full paper not accessible -- ACM DL blocked)

claim_text: On a 36-scenario benchmark requiring a model to reproduce a specific student's misconception-consistent behavior on a new task from one observed attempt, a fine-tuned GPT-3.5 showed no statistically significant difference from human tutors' performance (the paper's oracle upper bound), while un-fine-tuned baselines did not approach that ceiling.
quote_location: "there is no significant difference between the performances of GPT-3.5ft-SS and human tutors in TUTORSS (p > 0.05)" (Sec. 5.4/5.5, results)

claim_text: The benchmark this parity result comes from was built specifically because automated student-behavior-diagnosis methods (prior to LLM-based ones) showed a large accuracy gap against human tutors -- the parity result in N4-r3-07 closes a gap the field itself had flagged as large.
quote_location: "STUDENTSYN is a challenging benchmark for our problem setup, as evidenced by the huge performance gap between human tutors and automated methods proposed in [11]" (Sec. 4, benchmark description)

claim_text: Making an LLM-based dialogue knowledge-tracing model explicitly represent question difficulty, instead of relying only on opaque latent representations, produced a modest but consistent diagnostic-accuracy gain, and LLM-based diagnosis models in general outperformed classic deep-learning knowledge-tracing baselines (DKT, DKVMN, SAINT) on the same dialogue data.
quote_location: "our framework improves AUC from 64.89 to 65.25 (+0.36) on QATD2k and from 75.99 to 76.59 (+0.60) on MathDial ... LLM-based methods consistently outperform deep learning-based KT models" (Sec. 5.1, Table 1)

claim_text: In an exploratory case study, LLMs were used to turn raw keystroke-level programming-process data (44 CS1 students, 8 assignments) into natural-language process summaries and formative process-focused feedback, illustrating a route from process signals to diagnosis/feedback beyond derived time-on-task metrics -- reported as feasibility, not a measured learning-outcome gain.
quote_location: "we outline a case study where we have leveraged LLMs for automatically summarizing the programming process and for creating formative feedback on the programming process" (abstract)

claim_text: A validated two-tier diagnostic test (distinguishing lack-of-knowledge from a genuine misconception, not just a wrong answer) applied to 153 secondary-school science students found misconception prevalence differed significantly by grade level, demonstrating a portable, non-dialogue diagnostic-test methodology as an alternative to LLM/dialogue-based diagnosis.
quote_location: "Student misconceptions in science were found statistically significant among school grades, [F(2, 152) = 10.93, p<0.01]" (ERIC abstract/description)

claim_text: In 82 adult volunteers tracking a self-chosen daily habit (e.g. eating, drinking, activity) for up to 84 days with a self-report automaticity index, individual asymptotic-curve model fits show a median of 66 days (range 18-254) to reach 95% of one's automaticity plateau -- a very long and highly variable runway before a habit becomes self-sustaining.
quote_location: Abstract; p.1003 (Results, para 3)

claim_text: Across 140 identified single missed-practice occasions (55 participants), automaticity dropped by only 0.29 points on average the next day, and over a comparable 2-day window the increase after a missed opportunity (0.55 pts) was statistically indistinguishable (Wilcoxon, ns) from the increase when the behaviour was performed on both days (0.79 pts) -- a single lapse does not materially set back habit formation, and the timing of the lapse in the process did not moderate this (r=.099, p=.246, N=140).
quote_location: p.1005 (Results, 'missed opportunities' paragraph)

claim_text: Performing the target behaviour more consistently (not necessarily with zero missed days) was associated with a better-fitting individual automaticity curve, i.e. the predictor of durable habit formation in this dataset is consistency of repetition rather than unbroken perfection.
quote_location: Abstract; p.1003

claim_text: Across 3 archival field studies (Google search volume for 'diet', a university gym's check-in logs, and an online goal-commitment website's records), aspirational-behaviour initiation reliably spikes right after temporal landmarks -- the start of a new week, month, year, a semester, a birthday, a holiday -- attributed to landmarks psychologically demarcating a fresh 'mental accounting period' that relegates past lapses to the prior period.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: Across 3 samples (115 undergraduates; 120 young and older community adults; 45 parents of children with/without cancer), both the capacity to disengage effort from an unattainable goal and the capacity to reengage effort in a new goal independently predicted higher subjective well-being, and the two capacities showed interactive effects -- reengagement capacity, not merely disengagement, mattered for sustained goal pursuit.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: A narrative review of the skill/knowledge decay literature concludes decay is driven more by interference than by the mere passage of time, is highly dependent on task and situational factors, is smaller on complex tasks than on simple ones, and is reduced by more practice, elaborative rehearsal, and greater task mastery.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: On a real dataset of ~12 million Duolingo study sessions (~5.3 million unique user-word pairs over 2 weeks), an adaptive review-scheduling algorithm (Memorize) that times each review to the item's estimated recall probability achieves higher held-out likelihood of matching learners' actual reviewing/recall patterns than a fixed-uniform or a fixed-threshold reviewing schedule, i.e. matching review timing to the individual's estimated forgetting curve outperforms calendar-regular review timing in this retrospective evaluation.
quote_location: Section 4 (Experiments), Fig. 3 and surrounding text

claim_text: A PRISMA systematic review of 21 studies (2008-2021) on MOOC dropout finds that instructor-paced course designs contribute to attrition because 'the participant would give up when it was difficult to catch up,' while success in the first couple of weeks of a course is a documented predictor of eventual completion -- evidence that self-paced designs (allowing irregular-burst re-entry) fit sustained engagement better than fixed pacing for this population.
quote_location: Section 4 (Discussion), Table 8 and surrounding text

claim_text: The same systematic review's five-category framework for MOOC dropout factors names curiosity, motivation, self-regulation, and continuance intention -- grouped under 'Emotional Factor' -- as documented correlates of engagement and dropout across the reviewed literature, alongside course attributes, social status, cognitive ability, and learning-behaviour signals.
quote_location: Table 8 (Factors affecting MOOC performance)

claim_text: Across 3 controlled lab experiments, interruption-resumption skill trained on one primary/interrupting task pair transfers to a novel primary task -- both when the interrupting task is held constant and when it varies, and even when the experimental design minimizes the learner's ability to reconstruct the next step -- contradicting a prior finding, cited in the paper's own introduction, that such training does not transfer beyond the trained task pair.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: In a large-N observational study of commit timestamps across 86 open-source software projects (11,059 developers; cluster analysis on the 1,108 most active), roughly two-thirds of the most active developers cluster into regular 9-10am-to-6pm office-hour work patterns, while a distinct third cluster commits mostly from noon until midnight on both weekdays and weekends -- direct, population-matched (professional/OSS software developers) evidence of large real individual variation in when CS-adjacent skill-work happens, consistent with an irregular-bursts-toward-daily reality rather than a single normative schedule.
quote_location: Section on clustering results (Fig.2 and surrounding discussion)

claim_text: Comparing 10 expert and 10 novice Chinese mathematics teachers' noticing of the same classroom events: 'compared with novice teachers, expert teachers paid greater attention to developing mathematical and high-order thinking, and developing mathematics knowledge coherently, but paid less attention to teachers' guidance.'
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: Both expert and novice teachers in the same study attended similarly to students' self-exploratory learning and participation -- the expert margin was in emphasis and coherence of content-attention, not presence/absence of a whole category of noticing.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: Comparing 5 expert (cooperating) and 5 novice (student) teachers across planning, teaching and post-teaching interviews: 'expert teachers thought about learning from the perspective of the student and performed a cognitive analysis of each learning task during planning, which they adapted to the needs of students during teaching.'
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: In contrast, 'novices used specific lesson objectives to form structured lesson plans that they did not adapt to meet student needs during teaching' -- the margin is in-flight adaptation to the individual learner, not lesson preparation itself.
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: Comparing 2 novice and 4 expert elementary mathematics teachers via lesson videotapes and pre-class interviews, three elements distinguish expert lessons: 'rich agendas, consistent but flexible lesson structures, and explanations that meet the goals of clarifying concepts and procedures and having students learn and understand them.'
quote_location: Abstract

claim_text: A single expert vs. single novice 8th-grade math teacher, mobile-eye-tracked across two lessons each: 'the expert teacher distributed attention more evenly and identified a broader range of student needs, while the novice focused mainly on students who actively participated.'
quote_location: Abstract (n=1 expert, n=1 novice)

claim_text: Same pair, on the reasoning behind noticing: 'the expert engaged in deeper reasoning by linking student errors to prior learning experiences, whereas the novice attributed student confusion to disengagement' -- expert diagnosis reaches back into the learner's history, novice diagnosis stops at the surface behavior.
quote_location: Abstract (n=1 expert, n=1 novice)

claim_text: A second single-expert/single-novice mobile-eye-tracking case study, on attention across ability groups: 'the expert teacher distributed attention evenly across all groups during lessons, while the novice teacher focused primarily on strong students, then intermediate, and least on struggling students.'
quote_location: Abstract (n=1 expert, n=1 novice)

claim_text: Same study: 'significant transitions between strong and struggling or intermediate students occurred only in the expert teacher's lessons,' while the novice 'often returned to strong students after focusing on intermediate ones' -- the expert's attention graph reaches the struggling learner, the novice's loops back to the easy one.
quote_location: Abstract (n=1 expert, n=1 novice)

claim_text: Thematic analysis of 29 novice-expert feedback sessions in Chinese vocational-education teacher training: 'expert teachers of vocational subjects demonstrated a more problem-oriented, straightforward and structured approach to providing feedback than expert teachers of Chinese language and moral education' -- the feedback style the field ties to expertise varies by subject, not a single universal 'expert style.'
quote_location: ERIC description (abstract)

claim_text: Same study: 'when novice and expert teachers taught the same subject, the feedback provided was more informative and profound than feedback from expert teachers who teach a different subject to their novice peers' -- domain-match between coach and learner, not seniority alone, predicts feedback depth.
quote_location: ERIC description (abstract)

claim_text: Interview + interaction-recording study of 4 novice vocational-education teachers paired with expert mentors: 'expert-teachers' support not only provides feedback and suggestions for alternative teaching methods, but also encourages and maintains novice-teachers' learning,' and development is 'a complicated long-term process' in which novices 'internalised comments from expert teachers by active reflection and practice.'
quote_location: ERIC description (abstract)

claim_text: Pre/post control-group trial of a Chinese vocational-education teacher-development programme (41 experimental vs. 42 control novice teachers): the programme 'had significant effects on two sub-scales of teachers' efficacy (i.e. classroom management and student engagement) and one sub-scale of professional engagement (i.e. planned persistence)' -- the only professional-engagement sub-scale to move was the one that names staying in the work over time.

claim_text: Among students in a 6-week graduate robotics course, group membership in the Socratic-Guidance (SG) versus Prompt-Refinement (PR) LLM-tutor condition predicted adoption of 'understanding-driven' prompting during a later unconstrained-LLM course project: 13 of 29 SG-condition students vs 4 of 23 PR-condition students (chi-sq=8.14, p=.017); groups with more understanding-driven prompters scored higher on project understanding (beta=1.30, p=.025).
quote_location: Section 4.4 (p.11): cluster counts by condition -- Implementers (nSG=14, nPR=11), Understanding-driven (nSG=13, nPR=4), Debuggers (nSG=2, nPR=8), totals SG=29/PR=23 summing to the paper's stated 52 project-phase students; 'the distribution of students across clusters differed significantly by condition (chi2 = 8.14, p = 0.017)... students from the SG condition were more likely to enact Understanding-driven prompting patterns (nSG = 13, nPR = 4)'; Section 4.4: 'Groups with a higher number of Understanding-driven prompters achieved significantly higher understanding grades than groups with more Debuggers (beta = 1.30, p = 0.025)'

claim_text: One individual AI tutor (Gemma 4 31B) achieved GRE learning gains, on live tutored students, statistically equivalent to expert human tutoring's own measured learning gains (p=.044) at approximately 918x lower cost per percentage point of learning gain -- the same live-tutoring study as the pooled-AI-vs-human equivalence result, not the separate lesson-plan/practice-problem expert-rating study.
